newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico labor group CTM considers own pension fund.
newsitem.headline: Mexico labor group CTM considers own pension fund.

text.p: Mexico's largest labor organization is looking into launching its own pension fund, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"The Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM) is studying the possibility of drawing up its own pension fund," CTM Economic Adviser Alfonso Reyes told Reuters.

More than 10 million Mexican workers will be able to choose on July 1 from a number of competing pension funds, or Afores, where to deposit accounts currently held on their behalf by the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS).
Workers not choosing an Afore will by default see their funds retained by the central bank.
Reyes, also a congressman for the ruling Institutional revolutionary Party (PRI), said the CTM was planning to run its Afore as a joint venture with a private financial firm.
"It was a bad move not to have set one up," Reyes said, adding the CTM was legally within its rights to incorporate its own Afore.
The CTM has 11,000 affiliated labor unions with a total of more than 5.5 million members, and it has been a mainstay of the PRI's politcal machinery for for six decades.
Reyes denied the CTM would exert pressure on its members to opt for its own Afore and thus provide unfair competition for other funds.
"This does not mean all CTM workers would have the obligation to sign up with us," he said.
